steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Romantic music prioritised emotional expression: chromatic harmony, rubato, wider dynamic range and thicker textures created intensity and drama.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Chopin's piano music uses rubato (flexible tempo), elaborate ornamentation and harmonic chromaticism — it demands expressive, personal interpretation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Romantic orchestra expanded significantly: more brass (trombones, tuba), more woodwind (piccolo, cor anglais, bass clarinet), harp and percussion.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Late Romantic Requiems (Verdi, Fauré) combined liturgical text with dramatic orchestration — sacred music with theatrical emotional power.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how romantic music 1815-1910 are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use romantic music 1815-1910. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use romantic music 1815-1910 in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how romantic music 1815-1910 are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative langua | A practical application showing understanding of how romantic music 1815-1910 can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
